latest_release.name: v2.0.0
latest_release.body:
The major release that modernizes Freelens internals and unlocks further development.

v2.0.0 is a full internal rewrite of how Freelens is built, bundled, and tested. The application, its internal packages, and the extension API are now ESM-first, compiled by a single [Vite](https://vite.dev/) (electron-vite) pipeline directly from TypeScript sources, and tested with [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/). The UI runs on React 19, and the extension API has been redesigned as a specified, frozen contract, checked by porting real extensions to it. Most of the work is in the foundation, but the release also brings a standalone terminal, faster and more reliable cluster connections over HTTP/2, custom resources for users who may not list their definitions, verified binary downloads, and a long list of fixes. The extension API is **not compatible with v1 extensions**.

## What's new:

### Breaking Changes

* The extension API has been reorganized and is **not compatible with Freelens v1 extensions**. Extensions must be updated for v2 before they will load. Extensions may now be authored as either ESM or CommonJS, and must target React 19. See the [migration guide](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/blob/main/docs/extensions/migrating-from-v1.md). See #2102, #2110, #2304, #2465
* Extensions are now installed under the application data directory (`<userData>/extensions`) instead of `~/.freelens/extensions`. Extensions installed for v1 are not migrated and have to be installed again in their v2 versions. See #2400, #2467
* Renderer extensions get no guarantee of Node or Electron, `require()` included; Node work belongs in the main process, reached over IPC. See #2483, #2484
* Freelens is now ESM-first throughout — the main process, the renderer, all internal modules, and the extension API ship as ES modules. See #2102, #1718
* macOS 13 Ventura or later is required: Electron 44 no longer supports macOS 12. See #2864
* Removed the hierarchical-namespaces (HNC) tree view from the namespace details, together with the deprecated `@mui/lab` it was built on. See #2290
* Downloaded kubectl versions start at Kubernetes 1.22, and the China package mirror option is gone (the mirror stopped syncing). Older clusters use the bundled kubectl. See #2348, #2351

### New Features

* Open a terminal outside a cluster session: a standalone terminal page with its own tabs, reachable from the Welcome page, the Catalog, the hotbar and the command palette. It uses your own shell environment, `KUBECONFIG` and `kubectl`/`helm`, and the application's proxy as `HTTPS_PROXY`. See #2359, #2364
* Custom resources work for users who may list them but not their `CustomResourceDefinitions`: the sidebar, the list views and the details are built from the cluster's API discovery instead. See #2675, #2676, #2677, #2679
* Resource search matches across dashes and underscores, so `nginxingress` finds `nginx-ingress`. See #1937, #2711
* Cluster settings to skip the namespace authorization and metrics endpoint checks, for faster connection to large clusters. See #1699
* Terminal tabs show startup progress, including the kubectl download and its verification, instead of a stalled "Connecting ...". See #2357, #2358, #2367, #2368
* macOS natural text editing shortcuts in the embedded terminal (Option+Arrow word navigation, Command+Arrow line navigation, Command/Option+Delete). See #1051, #2338, #2354, #2355
* Installing an extension that is already installed and enabled offers to replace it, or to reinstall the same version, instead of failing with "Disable or uninstall it first". See #2798, #2799
* The Extensions page shows "Failed to load" for an enabled extension whose code did not load, with the process, the stage and the error in its tooltip, and labels each install as `verified`, `unverified` or `development` in colour. See #2780, #2787, #2788
* Downloaded log files have a timestamp in their name, so repeated downloads no longer overwrite each other. See #1884, #2565
